title: Chapter 300: The Artist
html:
Xu Yin slowly emerged behind Chen Ge. Human and ghost charged the old woman together, making every wrinkle on her face contract.

When Chen Ge left Room 304 and entered the shadows, the old woman’s dry lips curled into a smile. Before she could act, however, a man in a half-red shirt lunged at her.

“So painful!”

Blood seeped from Xu Yin’s wounds as he dropped to all fours like a feral beast. The old woman’s smile froze. With speed utterly at odds with her age, she dissolved into a shadow and fled down the stairs.

“Didn’t you ask me to follow you?!” The hammer landed heavily at the spot where the old lady had stood a moment ago, and the sound echoed throughout the building.

“None of you are escaping me tonight!”

Xu Yin and Chen Ge raced after her.

Footsteps thundered through the stairwell. The steps seemed endless, and for the first time the old woman felt the building stretch impossibly tall. This was probably the most terrifying night of her existence.

The exit was just before her.

The shadow fled with all her strength. She was only an ordinary Lingering Spirit, and the sight of Xu Yin’s half-red shirt had nearly made her soul scatter from fear.

“Stand right there!” Chen Ge called after her.

Xu Yin was marginally faster. Just as the shadow reached freedom, he seized one of her arms. She shuddered, tore the limb from her own body without hesitation, and fled into the darkness beyond the building.

I need more training. I was far too slow.Chen Ge sighed regretfully.

When he turned toward Xu Yin, the severed arm had already vanished, while the bloodstain across the ghost’s shirt appeared larger.

Perhaps it won’t be a terrible thing if Xu Yin becomes a Red Specter.Chen Ge looked down at the dark residential area. Since we’ve met, I can’t just sit idle. After I find the drawer, I’ll come back to deal with the old lady’s lingering wish.

With Xu Yin beside him, Chen Ge returned to the third floor and called the agent. When she failed to answer, he sent a message requesting a reply. He wished to ‘thank’ her personally for the warning. Why won’t she answer?

Holding the phone in his left hand, Chen Ge dragged the hammer back into Room 304 with his right. I’ve searched the living room and the first bedroom. Only the innermost room remains, and every spirit here has tried to keep me away from it.

The last room was locked from inside, a problem one swing of the hammer quickly solved. If the bedroom was secured from within, could the gambler’s missing arm be inside?

Chen Ge forced open the door and entered. The tiny bedroom was half consumed by a large bookcase and desk; a rusted miniature refrigerator and tattered sleeping mat occupied most of what remained.

The mat’s frayed edges show frequent use. But there’s a proper bed in the other room. Why did someone insist on sleeping here? What frightened him?

The atmosphere differed completely from the rest of the apartment. No chill tainted the air, and neither drawers nor shelves had been boarded shut.

The working table and shelf are perfectly clean. They look like they’ve been cleaned daily.

Studying the immaculate bookcase, Chen Ge entertained a strange thought. It feels as though the Lingering Spirits clean this room. Are the ghosts here obsessed with tidiness?

The shelves held books on creating comics.

How to create a successful comic series, how to build an exciting world, an introduction to human anatomy…

These books don’t seem to fit the previous tenants’ identities, so has this place played host to a fourth tenant?

After replacing the books, Chen Ge found a box of discarded drafts beneath the shelves. Many had been crumpled or torn apart, yet someone had painstakingly reconstructed every page with tape.

Why preserve all these rejected drafts?Chen Ge lifted the thick stack and began reading. Something was wrong with every character. The artist had clearly tried to make them cute and commercially appealing, but the results were profoundly disturbing.

The artist was certainly no professional. His characters lacked lively expressions; many stared with empty eyes, while others appeared frozen in terror. His efforts to improve and satisfy popular tastes were obvious, but his sense of beauty was fundamentally different. Even when copying famous characters, he made them resemble female corpses.

It’s a kind of talent to be able to draw every picture as scary as these.

Chen Ge set down the drafts and found a thin, yellow-covered notebook at the back of the shelf. It was a ledger recording the artist’s weekly expenses and income from his work.

As Chen Ge read, his frown deepened. The comic artist had also lived in Room 304, apparently sharing the apartment and renting only this cramped bedroom.

His life had been desperately hard. Despite his love of comics, three years of drawing earned him only twelve hundred yuan. One thousand came from the elderly landlady, apparently his sole fan. The remaining two hundred came from drawing portraits beneath a bridge.

Unfortunately, he rendered a living customer like a corpse and was chased for several blocks. After the police intervened, the customer gave him two hundred yuan in compensation.

Passion alone sustained him. He kept his monthly expenses below four hundred yuan and clung to the belief that success would eventually come. Cruel reality never rewarded that faith; even on his final day, his work remained unappreciated. Folded into the ledger’s last page was a newspaper article about a middle-aged man who died saving a drowning boy. The report never named him.

This is different from the other spirits. Just how many tenants has Room 304 had?Chen Ge replaced the notebook and walked to the desk. It’s facing away from the living room. This should be the table mentioned in the black phone.

Drawing tools covered the desk as though awaiting their owner’s return. Beneath its surface were three drawers. Chen Ge opened the first and found it filled with pencils and pens.

“Not this one.” The second drawer overflowed with rejection letters addressed to the middle-aged artist.

Then Chen Ge grasped the third handle and pulled with all his strength. The drawer did not move.
